component: Pump Portion of Motor Pump Set
steps: Isolate power to the motor pump set and shut off all valves.
Drain the pump casing completely.
Disassemble the pump portion, carefully removing the casing cover, impeller, and any associated components.
Thoroughly clean all internal components.
Visually inspect the impeller, casing ring, and casing cover for signs of wear, damage, or foreign material.
Measure the clearance between the impeller and the casing ring, and between the impeller and the casing cover (using feeler gauges or manufacturer-specified tools).
Compare measured clearances to manufacturer's specifications.
Replace any worn-out parts (impeller, casing ring, casing cover, seals, bearings) as necessary.
Reassemble the pump, ensuring all fasteners are torqued to specification and clearances are within tolerance.
Perform a functional test after reassembly.
expected_result: Pump internal clearances are within manufacturer's specifications, and all worn parts are replaced, restoring optimal pump efficiency and preventing rubbing.
safety_warnings: Ensure power is disconnected and locked out before starting work.
Be aware of residual pressure or hot liquids.

steps: Isolate power to the motor pump set and shut off all valves.
Drain the pump casing completely.
Disassemble the pump, removing all components that come into contact with the pumped liquid (impeller, casing, shaft, seals).
Thoroughly clean and visually inspect each component for signs of abnormal corrosion (pitting, uniform attack, crevice corrosion) or erosion (material loss, surface roughening).
Document the type and extent of observed damage.
Identify the specific liquid being pumped and its chemical/physical properties (pH, temperature, abrasiveness).
Consult pump manufacturer's material compatibility charts or a materials specialist to determine if the current component materials are suitable for the liquid.

If abnormal corrosion/erosion is observed and material incompatibility is confirmed, identify and order replacement components made from a more resistant material (e.g., stainless steel, bronze, specific alloys).
Replace the affected components with the new, suitable material parts.
Reassemble the pump, ensuring all seals and gaskets are new and correctly installed.
Perform a functional test after reassembly.
expected_result: Pump components are made of materials suitable for the liquid being pumped, preventing premature failure due to corrosion or erosion, and extending pump service life.
safety_warnings: Ensure power is disconnected and locked out before starting work.
Be aware of residual pressure or hot/hazardous liquids.
